title: Sudan's Burhan Rejects US Visa Ultimatum, Vows to Continue War Against RSF
detail: September 26, 2026 — Sudanese army chief and Sovereignty Council head Abdel Fattah al-Burhan publicly rejected Washington's decision to withhold his UN General Assembly visa unless he accepted a 90-day unconditional ceasefire proposed by US Senior Adviser Massad Boulos. Skipping his UN address (Foreign Minister Mohieldin Salem spoke in his place), Burhan instead addressed a crowd of sports figures and content creators at Khartoum Stadium: 'We do not want a visa to any country, nor do we want their permission, nor do we want anything,' and pledged to keep pursuing the Rapid Support Forces 'across the entire country' until it is eliminated. The remarks — his first public response since the visa dispute broke into the open around Sep 22-24 and drew condemnation from Sudanese civil society and journalists as a violation of UN convention — mark a hardening of his position against the US-brokered truce track.

title: Hamas Slams Board of Peace for Excluding UNRWA From Gaza Reconstruction
detail: September 25-26, 2026 — Trump's Board of Peace said UNRWA will have no role in its $2.45 billion Gaza recovery plan, stating it will work only with partners it deems 'trusted' and that the UN Palestinian refugee agency does not meet that standard — echoing a longstanding Israeli demand to sideline UNRWA. Hamas spokesperson Hazem Qassem called the decision 'a complete alignment with the Zionist position,' accusing the Board of trying to end UNRWA's operations and eliminate the right of return. An ABC News investigation published Sep 25 reported the Board has in fact held multiple undisclosed meetings with UNRWA, with Gaza's Board-supervised administration privately telling the agency 'I don't know how I can succeed without you.' Former UNRWA chief Philippe Lazzarini warned removing the agency, still Gaza's largest aid, health and education provider, would be 'devastating' for the territory nearly a year into the ceasefire.

title: Trump Rejects Iran's Seven-Day Hormuz Roadmap; Araghchi Says Tehran 'Will Not Back Down'
detail: September 26, 2026 — President Trump rejected the seven-day roadmap Iran submitted a day earlier, telling reporters Tehran wants a deal 'because they are losing so badly' and that its proposal 'would not be acceptable.' US UN Ambassador Mike Waltz called the offer 'a pretty cynical attempt to put something on the table that they knew was unacceptable,' citing the 146-country UN vote condemning Iran's attacks on civilian shipping. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi responded that Iran 'will not back down' on its conditions and that 'only a negotiated solution' can end the standoff, while Iran's Rezaei said Tehran remained 'fully prepared for the war to be resumed' if talks fail. Despite the rejection, Trump said a further round of contact was likely 'in the very near future.'

title: UN-AU Task Force Meets in New York; Congolese Authorities Move to Convene National Dialogue
detail: September 26, 2026 — The UN-African Union Joint Task Force on Peace and Security held its 27th consultative meeting in New York. The joint communiqué noted the Congolese authorities' decision to convene a national dialogue, with emphasis on making the process inclusive.
